question: Assess whether small-scale tomato farming in Kirinyaga County is worth investigating, considering wholesale market prices in Wang'uru and Wakulima, certified seed and drip irrigation production costs, river water abstraction quotas, and aggregator offtake terms.

decision.note: Evidence checklist coverage, not a probability of success, crop yield, or profitability.

rationale: Nexus evaluated 4 record(s), but the available evidence failed minimum sufficiency requirements (coverage score 75/100). Essential agronomic, pricing, or water access data is missing or unverified. Do not commit capital without verified field data.

evidence.source_name: Wang'uru & Wakulima Wholesale Market Price Bulletin
evidence.title: Kirinyaga tomato wholesale prices by seasonal window
evidence.claim: Wholesale tomato prices in Wang'uru market averaged 78-95 KES/kg during dry season (July-Sept) but dropped to 42-55 KES/kg during peak rain glut.
evidence.detail: Survey of wholesale buyers across Wang'uru and Nairobi Wakulima markets shows Grade 1 Anna F1 and Kilele F1 tomatoes fetched 85 KES/kg median in dry harvest. Peak harvest in Mwea creates 40% price deflation without cold-chain storage.
quality_flags: Wholesale price varies by grade; transport costs to Nairobi Wakulima (~12 KES/crate) must be accounted for.

evidence.title: Open-market price volatility and payment terms
evidence.claim: Middlemen and informal aggregators in Wang'uru pay cash on delivery but enforce a 15-20% rejection rate on uncalibrated crates.
evidence.detail: Without a formal offtake agreement, smallholders selling at farmgate absorb rejection costs and lack price protection during harvest surges.
quality_flags: Rejection criteria depend on grading calibration.

evidence.source_name: KALRO Horticulture Research Institute - Production Budget
evidence.title: One-acre hybrid tomato production cost breakdown
evidence.claim: Total production cost for 1 acre of open-field hybrid tomatoes (Anna F1 / Kilele) is approximately 195,000 to 240,000 KES.
evidence.detail: Breakdown per acre: certified seeds (18,000 KES), seedling nursery propagation (12,000 KES), land preparation & ridging (20,000 KES), basal & topdressing fertilizer (45,000 KES), pest/disease chemical spray program (38,000 KES), trellising stakes & twine (32,000 KES), labor & harvesting (40,000 KES). Yield potential under good management: 18-25 tons/acre.
quality_flags: Yield is contingent on pest management (Tuta absoluta, bacterial wilt) and reliable irrigation.

evidence.source_name: Water Resources Authority (WRA) Mt. Kenya Sub-Region
evidence.title: River Thiba & Nyamindi seasonal abstraction quotas
evidence.claim: Unregulated furrow water abstraction is prohibited during dry months; drip irrigation with permitted storage weir is mandatory.
evidence.detail: Dry-season farming requires an on-farm water reservoir (min. 150m3) or shallow borehole. Pumping fuel costs add 22,000-30,000 KES per cycle if grid electricity is unavailable.
quality_flags: Permit application lead time is 4-6 weeks.

conflicts.explanation: Wholesale market pricing indicates favorable gross revenues, but buyer offtake records indicate severe rejection rates (15-20%) and informal price deflation without binding purchase contracts.

missing_information: Confirm the source dates and grading methodology for wholesale price claims.
Verify farm-specific water abstraction quotas and on-farm buffer storage capacity.
Obtain written offtake terms or binding purchase agreements before transplanting.
next_actions: Inspect the cited source URLs and verify date and grade relevance to Kirinyaga.
Obtain current local supplier quotations for drip irrigation and certified seed.
Re-run the investigation once farm-specific cost and water permits are established.

financial_metrics.sensitivity_notes: At wholesale spot price of 85 KES/kg, enterprise gross margin is 85.7%. If sold during peak harvest rain glut at 45 KES/kg with 20% aggregator crate rejection, gross revenue falls to 774,000 KES, reducing operating margin to 72.2%. Production remains cash-positive above 12.1 KES/kg breakeven. Primary financial exposure is informal aggregator rejection and lack of cold storage.

risk_matrix.title: Informal Aggregator Offtake Volatility & Crate Rejection
risk_matrix.impact: Middlemen in Wang'uru enforce 15–20% crate rejections on uncalibrated produce, shifting grading risk onto smallholders.
risk_matrix.mitigation: Require binding offtake contracts with transparent Grade 1/2 calibration before loan disbursement.

risk_matrix.title: Water Resources Authority (WRA) Abstraction Restrictions
risk_matrix.impact: Unregulated furrow water pumping from Rivers Thiba/Nyamindi is prohibited during dry months; permits are mandatory.
risk_matrix.mitigation: Mandate valid WRA abstraction permits and verify on-farm water reservoir capacity (min. 150m³ storage weir).

risk_matrix.title: Tuta Absoluta & Bacterial Wilt Vulnerability
risk_matrix.impact: Severe leafminer infestation and soil-borne wilt can reduce harvestable yield by 40–60% without preventive rotation.
risk_matrix.mitigation: Underwrite loan conditional on KALRO-certified hybrid seeds (Anna F1 / Kilele) and structured IPM spray calendar.

risk_matrix.title: Seasonal Rain Harvest Price Deflation
risk_matrix.impact: Peak harvest supply in Mwea causes open-market prices to plunge from 85 KES/kg to 42–55 KES/kg.
risk_matrix.mitigation: Structure planting calendar for off-peak harvest window (July–September) using drip irrigation to capture high prices.

risk_matrix.title: Contradiction in market_vs_offtake
risk_matrix.impact: Wholesale market pricing indicates favorable gross revenues, but buyer offtake records indicate severe rejection rates (15-20%) and informal price deflation without binding purchase contracts.
risk_matrix.mitigation: Require human field verification and signed purchase orders before capital commitment.
